signal.name: ECMWF warm-winter forecast versus Dutch TTF
signal.hypothesis: A high-probability August ECMWF SEAS5 forecast for above-upper-tercile DJF temperatures across a fixed European gas-demand region should create a bearish weather impulse in the Dutch TTF December-January-February strip relative to matched August release windows.
target_assets: ICE Endex Dutch TTF December, January and February monthly futures
signal.horizon: Primary: five ICE trading sessions after the verified forecast release; secondary: 20 sessions and November 30 diagnostics
applicable_regimes: normal European gas-market functioning with weather-sensitive winter risk premium
liquid TTF winter contracts before the heating season
invalid_regimes: war, sanctions or infrastructure disruption dominating weather information
extreme storage or policy intervention overwhelming temperature demand
forecast probability reconstructed from chart colors rather than machine-readable data
signal.mechanism: Warmer European winter expectations reduce expected heating demand and weather-risk premium, which should pressure the winter TTF strip all else equal.
signal.decay_mechanism: The weather forecast may be anticipated, revised, poorly calibrated at long lead, or overwhelmed by storage, supply, geopolitics and power-sector demand.
signal.canonical_rule: Using the August-initialized ECMWF SEAS5 ensemble, calculate the area-weighted probability that DJF mean 2m temperature is in the model's upper tercile over 35-60N and 10W-30E. Trigger a short-TTF research event only when that probability is at least 60 percent. Enter at the next ICE settlement after the verified public release and use an equal-weight December-January-February monthly strip. Exit after five ICE trading sessions; subtract EUR 0.05/MWh round trip.
signal.deactivation_rule: Reject or redesign if the machine-readable forecast cannot be reproduced point in time, if at least ten independent historical or prospective events show non-negative after-cost TTF returns relative to the matched benchmark, or if the result is confined to one supply regime.
signal.benchmark: Same-year-season unconditional five-session TTF DJF-strip returns sampled from matched August dates, with release-year and supply-regime controls.
signal.data_source: ECMWF/Copernicus seasonal forecast and hindcast fields plus point-in-time ICE Endex Dutch TTF settlement history. The supplied chart and screenshot are source evidence only.
signal.notes: The uploaded map is probabilistic and visually warm across much of Europe, but it does not provide a machine-readable regional probability. The embedded Polymarket El Nino claim is excluded. Historical ICE settlement data is not available in the repository, so no market-performance claim is made.
